events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east central Ohio, including the following
areas, Belmont, Carroll, Columbiana, Coshocton, Guernsey, Harrison,
Jefferson OH, Monroe, Muskingum, Noble and Tuscarawas,
Pennsylvania, including the following areas, Allegheny, Beaver,
Fayette, Greene, Higher Elevations of Fayette, Higher Elevations of
Westmoreland, Washington and Westmoreland, and West Virginia,
including the following areas, Brooke, Eastern Preston, Eastern
Tucker, Hancock, Marion, Marshall, Monongalia, Ohio, Preston,
Ridges of Eastern Monongalia and Northwestern Preston, Western
Tucker and Wetzel.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall of 1 to 2 inches is forecast across much of
the watch area through Monday morning, with isolated totals of up
to 3 inches possible. Combined with an already saturated ground,
instances of flash flooding are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Ohio...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Wells and Adams Counties.

Saint Marys River near Decatur affecting Van Wert, Allen IN and
Adams Counties.

Kankakee River at Davis affecting St. Joseph, La Porte and Starke
Counties.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne affecting
Allen IN County.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN, Wabash,
Logansport...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the Kankakee River...including Davis...Minor flooding is
forecast.
For the Saint Marys River...including Decatur, St. Mary's River near
Fort Wayne...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Saint Marys River near Decatur.

* WHEN...Until late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At 23.5 feet, Many east side city streets and county
roads are flooded. Evacuation of east side residents near Bellmont
High School becomes necessary.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:10 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 23.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:10 AM EDT Sunday was 23.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Thursday morning and continue falling to 14.5 feet Friday
morning.
- Flood stage is 17.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northern Belmont County in east central Ohio...
East Central Coshocton County in east central Ohio...
Northeastern Guernsey County in east central Ohio...
Southern Harrison County in east central Ohio...
Southwestern Jefferson OH County in east central Ohio...
Southern Tuscarawas County in east central Ohio...

* WHEN...Until 245 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1147 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated light rain across the
warned area, but additional approaching heavy rain may continue
andy ongoing flooding. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the warned area. Between 2.5 and 3.5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall of up to an inch is possible
this afternoon.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Martins Ferry, St. Clairsville, Freeport, Newcomerstown,
Bridgeport, Antrim, Flushing, Adena, Dillonvale, Brookside, Port
Washington, Mount Pleasant, Holloway, New Athens, Harrisville,
Piedmont, Tippecanoe and Gilmore.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1142 AM EDT, Soppler radar indicated that rain was ending across
the warned area. Earlier, emergency management reported several
instances of flash flooding across the warned area. Between 1.5 and
2.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1.0
inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Washington, Canonsburg, Avella, Wolfdale, McGovern, Bentleyville,
East Washington, New Eagle, Baidland, Houston, Ellsworth,
Claysville, Deemston, Eighty Four, Cokeburg, Hickory, Beallsville
and West Alexander.
